name: viterbi
description: A soft-decision Viterbi decoder for the K=7, rate-1/2 convolutional code with generator polynomials G0 = 133, G1 = 171 (octal), the standard code used by IEEE 802.11a/g, DVB, and CCSDS/NASA.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Soft-decision Viterbi decoder for the K=7, rate-1/2 convolutional code with generator polynomials G0=133, G1=171 (octal), the de-facto standard code used by IEEE 802.11a/g, DVB, and CCSDS/NASA. It finds the maximum-likelihood transmitted bit sequence through the 64-state code trellis and corrects channel errors. The decoder is fully parallel: all 64 add-compare-select (ACS) butterflies are evaluated every clock for one trellis step per clock, with each coded bit arriving as an SW-bit soft confidence symbol whose branch metric is the soft correlation distance. Path metrics are normalized every step by subtracting the running minimum so a fixed metric width never overflows. Survivor decisions (1 bit per state) are written to a RAM-based traceback memory each step; the frame is traced back from the best (minimum path-metric) state to recover the decoded bits, with the survivor memory mapping to FPGA BRAM. It is a frame-based decoder: stream a frame of soft symbol pairs (in_valid/in_last), then trace back the whole frame and stream decoded bits out (out_valid/out_bit), oldest first, at roughly two clocks per decoded bit.
key_decisions: Fully-parallel ACS: all 64 trellis-state butterflies (2^(K-1) states) are evaluated every clock, one trellis step per clock, modeled as per-state generated combinational hardware plus an explicit reduction.
Soft-decision branch-metric unit: each coded bit arrives as an SW-bit confidence symbol and the branch metric is the soft (correlation) distance rather than a hard Hamming distance.
Path-metric normalization every step by subtracting the running 64-way minimum, so a fixed metric width never overflows (the subtract-minimum scheme).

RAM-based traceback: survivor decisions (1 bit/state) are written to memory each step and the frame is traced back from the best state; the survivor memory maps to FPGA BRAM (sdpram_16384x1 + sdpram_1024x16).

Block/frame decoder (accept the whole frame, then trace it back) chosen so the traceback is simple and bit-exact, rather than a continuous multi-bank streaming traceback; frame length must be <= MAXLEN with a K-1 zero tail terminating the trellis in state 0.
The code (K=7, G0=133, G1=171) is fixed; only the soft symbol width SW and the maximum frame length MAXLEN are configurable parameters.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.
